# Audio Signal Processing Apparatus for Three-Dimensional Image Presentation

An audio signal processing apparatus is provided that comprises a receiver configured to obtain an audio signal. This audio signal contains audio data for at least a first audio object that is associated with a three-dimensional image. In this way, the apparatus is able to handle sound content that corresponds directly to visual elements presented as part of a three-dimensional scene.

In addition to the audio data itself, the received audio signal also includes depth position data. This depth position data indicates a target depth position for the first audio object, thereby specifying where, along the depth dimension, the audio object is intended to be perceived relative to the viewer.

To ensure that the audio can be reproduced in a manner appropriate to the display being used, the apparatus further comprises a determiner. The determiner is arranged to establish a visual rendering depth range for a target three-dimensional display that is used to present the three-dimensional image. This visual rendering depth range reflects the depth capabilities and characteristics of the particular display device on which the image is shown.

The apparatus additionally includes a mapper, which converts the target depth position into a rendering depth position for the audio object. Significantly, this mapping operation is dependent on the visual rendering depth range established by the determiner. As a result, the conversion takes into account the specific depth range supported by the target display, allowing the audio rendering to be tailored to the display in use.

Through this mechanism, the mapper is able to adjust the positions of audio object sound sources so that they match the depth positions of the corresponding visual objects displayed by the three-dimensional display. Consequently, the perceived location of each sound source is brought into alignment with the visual presentation, producing a coherent and immersive audiovisual experience in which audio and image depth are consistently reproduced.

# Synchronizing Audio Object Positioning with Three-Dimensional Visual Displays

## Overview

The apparatus described herein addresses a significant challenge in modern audio-visual systems: ensuring that the positioning of audio objects is accurately synchronized with three-dimensional visual displays. As immersive media experiences become increasingly prevalent, the alignment between what viewers see and what they hear plays a critical role in creating convincing and realistic presentations. This apparatus provides a technical solution to achieve precise correspondence between audio sound sources and their associated visual elements within a three-dimensional space.

## System Components and Operation

At the core of the apparatus is a **receiver**, which is configured to obtain two essential types of information. First, it acquires the audio data associated with one or more audio objects. Second, it retrieves target depth position information, which specifies where each audio object should be perceived within the depth dimension of the presentation. This target depth position corresponds to the intended location of the sound source relative to the viewer.

Working in conjunction with the receiver is a **determiner**, which is responsible for establishing the visual rendering depth range of the display. Because different displays possess varying capabilities for rendering three-dimensional content, the determiner assesses the specific depth range over which the display can present visual objects. This ensures that the system accounts for the actual physical and technical constraints of the display being used.

The final key component is a **mapper**, which performs the conversion of target depth positions into corresponding rendering positions. Using the visual rendering depth range established by the determiner, the mapper translates each audio object's intended target depth into an appropriate rendering position that fits within the display's capabilities. This mapping process ensures that the audio positioning is scaled and adapted to match the visual depth characteristics of the specific display.

## Benefits and Applications

By coordinating these components, the apparatus ensures that the sound sources of audio objects are accurately aligned with the depth positions of their corresponding visual objects. When a viewer perceives an object appearing at a particular depth on the display, the associated sound is rendered to emanate from that same perceived location. This precise alignment eliminates the disorienting mismatch that can occur when audio and visual cues are inconsistent.

The result is a marked improvement in the coherence and realism of combined audio-visual three-dimensional presentations. Viewers experience a more immersive and believable environment, in which auditory and visual elements work together seamlessly. This approach is particularly valuable in applications such as three-dimensional cinema, virtual reality, augmented reality, and advanced home entertainment systems, where maintaining consistency between audio and visual depth is essential for delivering a high-quality, engaging experience.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a patent about synchronizing audio object depth positioning with 3D display rendering capabilities.
counterfactuals.output:
# Abstract

A system and method for synchronizing audio object depth positioning with three-dimensional (3D) display rendering capabilities are disclosed. The system receives audio content comprising one or more audio objects, each associated with spatial metadata defining a position in a three-dimensional space, including a depth coordinate relative to a display plane. A rendering coordinator determines display capability parameters of a connected 3D display device, including a supported depth range, disparity limits, and rendering resolution. Based on the determined display capabilities, the system maps the depth coordinate of each audio object to a corresponding visual depth position of a rendered 3D object, thereby maintaining perceptual alignment between the perceived spatial location of a sound source and its visually rendered counterpart. In some embodiments, an audio processor dynamically adjusts spatial audio parameters, including inter-channel level differences, delay, and reverberation, to reposition an audio object such that its perceived depth corresponds to the visual depth constrained by the display device. The system may further include a latency compensation module that temporally aligns audio rendering with display frame output to minimize audiovisual mismatch during dynamic scene changes. By adapting audio depth cues to the specific rendering envelope of heterogeneous 3D display devices—including autostereoscopic, light-field, and head-mounted displays—the disclosed system provides an immersive and consistent audiovisual experience across diverse hardware platforms.

counterfactuals.output:
# Technical Description: Depth-Aware Audio Object Rendering System for Three-Dimensional Display Environments

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to audio-visual signal processing systems, and more particularly to methods and apparatus for associating audio objects with depth position data derived from three-dimensional (3D) image content, and for adaptively mapping such depth positions to the visual rendering capabilities of a target display device.

## Background

Conventional audio systems reproduce sound using channel-based configurations (e.g., stereo, 5.1, 7.1 surround) in which audio signals are pre-assigned to fixed loudspeaker positions. Object-based audio systems, by contrast, represent sound sources as discrete audio objects, each accompanied by metadata describing positional and behavioral attributes. However, prior systems have inadequately synchronized the perceived depth of audio objects with the perceived depth of corresponding visual elements in stereoscopic and autostereoscopic 3D displays, resulting in spatial dissonance between what a viewer sees and hears.

## Summary of the Invention

The invention provides a system in which each audio object is associated with **depth position data** that corresponds to the depth (Z-axis) position of a related visual object within a 3D image. The system further includes a **mapping module** that transforms authored depth positions into rendered depth positions based on the **visual rendering depth range** of the specific display on which the content is presented.

---

## Detailed Description

### 1. Audio Object Structure

An audio object comprises:

- **Audio essence**: one or more audio waveform signals (e.g., PCM samples representing the sound source).
- **Positional metadata**, including:
  - Lateral position (X-axis)
  - Vertical position (Y-axis)
  - **Depth position (Z-axis)** — a value representing the distance of the sound source relative to a reference plane, typically the display surface.
- **Behavioral metadata**: gain, size/spread, priority, and rendering constraints.

The depth position value may be expressed as a normalized coordinate, for example within a range of **-1.0 to +1.0**, where:
- **0.0** corresponds to the plane of the display screen,
- **negative values** correspond to positions behind the screen (into the display), and
- **positive values** correspond to positions in front of the screen (toward the viewer).

### 2. Derivation of Depth Position Data from 3D Images

The depth position associated with an audio object may be obtained through one or more of the following methods:

1. **Disparity/parallax extraction**: For stereoscopic content, the horizontal disparity between the left-eye and right-eye images of a visual object is measured. Disparity is inversely related to depth; the extracted disparity value is converted into a depth position value.

2. **Depth map sampling**: For content accompanied by a depth map (Z-buffer), the depth value at the pixel location of the visual object is sampled directly.

3. **Authoring-time assignment**: During content production, a human operator or automated tool associates each audio object with the on-screen visual element that produces the sound, and the visual element's depth is propagated to the audio object metadata.

The depth position data may be **time-varying**, tracking a moving visual object across successive frames such that the audio object's perceived depth follows the visual object's trajectory.

### 3. Display Depth Range Characterization

Different 3D displays possess different **visual rendering depth ranges** — the span of perceivable depth that a display can reproduce without inducing excessive viewer discomfort (e.g., from accommodation-vergence conflict). This range is defined by:

- A **maximum negative depth** (Z_far) — furthest comfortable depth behind the screen.
- A **maximum positive depth** (Z_near) — nearest comfortable depth in front of the screen.

The display's rendering depth range may be:
- Retrieved from display capability metadata (e.g., via EDID or an equivalent descriptor),
- Configured by the user, or
- Determined by the display's physical parameters (size, pixel pitch, expected viewing distance).

### 4. Depth Position Mapping

The core of the invention is a mapping process that transforms the **authored depth position** (Z_auth) of an audio object into a **rendered depth position** (Z_rend) appropriate to the target display's rendering depth range.

In one embodiment, a **linear mapping** is applied:

```
Z_rend = Z_auth × (R_display / R_reference)
```

where:
- `R_reference` is the depth range assumed during content authoring,
- `R_display` is the visual rendering depth range of the target display.

More generally, the mapping may employ a **piecewise or nonlinear transfer function** that:

- **Preserves the screen plane** (Z = 0 maps to Z = 0), maintaining registration between on-screen audio and visual objects;
- **Compresses depth values** approaching the display's limits to avoid clipping, using a soft-knee compression curve;
- **Applies asymmetric scaling** for the near (in-front) and far (behind) regions, reflecting the display's differing forward and rearward depth capabilities.

An example nonlinear mapping:

```
Z_rend = Z_max × tanh(k × Z_auth)
```

where `Z_max` is the display's corresponding depth limit and `k` is a scaling constant controlling compression aggressiveness.

### 5. Audio Rendering Based on Mapped Depth

The rendered depth position Z_rend is provided to an **audio rendering engine**, which reproduces the audio object with a spatial impression consistent with the mapped depth. Depending on the reproduction system, depth cues are synthesized through:

- **Loudspeaker arrays**: Distance rendering via inter-object level differences, direct-to-reverberant ratio adjustment, and wavefront curvature synthesis (e.g., wave field synthesis).
- **Headphone/binaural reproduction**: Application of distance-dependent Head-Related Transfer Functions (HRTFs), near-field parallax cues, and distance-based reverberation.

By deriving the audio depth cues from the same depth range as the visual presentation, the system maintains **audio-visual spatial coherence**: an object that appears to protrude from the screen is simultaneously heard as being closer to the viewer, and an object receding into the display is heard as more distant.

### 6. System Architecture

A representative system includes:

1. A **content decoder** that separates audio objects, associated metadata, and 3D image data from an incoming bitstream.
2. A **depth analysis module** (where depth is not pre-authored) that extracts depth from the image data.
3. A **display interrogation module** that determines the target display's visual rendering depth range.
4. A **depth mapping module** that computes Z_rend from Z_auth and the display range.
5. An **audio rendering engine** that generates loudspeaker or headphone feeds using the mapped depth positions.
6. A **video rendering engine** that drives the 3D display, operating in synchronization with the audio rendering engine.

---

## Advantages

- **Perceptual coherence** between audio depth and visual depth across heterogeneous 3D displays.
- **Display-adaptive rendering** that automatically adjusts audio depth to each device's comfortable depth range without re-authoring content.
- **Backward compatibility**, since audio objects without depth metadata may default to a screen-plane position (Z = 0).
- **Content portability**, enabling a single authored asset to be optimally rendered on displays ranging from mobile stereoscopic screens to large-format cinema systems.

## Claims (Illustrative)

1. A method comprising: receiving an audio object associated with depth position data corresponding to a depth of a visual object in a three-dimensional image; determining a visual rendering depth range of a display; mapping the depth position data to a rendered depth position based on the visual rendering depth range; and rendering the audio object according to the rendered depth position.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the mapping preserves a screen-plane depth value and compresses depth values approaching a limit of the visual rendering depth range.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the depth position data is derived from disparity between left-eye and right-eye images of the visual object.

---

*Note: This document is a technical description intended to illustrate the structure and content of an invention disclosure. It should not be relied upon as legal patent advice; consult a qualified patent professional for filing.*

# Abstract

An apparatus for processing spatial audio data in conjunction with visual display content is disclosed. The apparatus comprises a receiver configured to receive audio data comprising one or more audio objects having associated depth positions, and depth data representing depth positions of one or more visual objects. A determiner is coupled to the receiver and configured to determine a depth range of a display device on which the visual objects are to be rendered. A mapper is operatively coupled to the receiver and the determiner and is configured to adjust the depth positions of the audio objects to correspond with the depth positions of respective corresponding visual objects, wherein the adjustment is performed in dependence upon the determined depth range of the display device. The apparatus thereby provides spatial coherence between rendered audio objects and their corresponding visual objects, improving the perceptual alignment of auditory and visual cues presented to a user across display devices having differing depth rendering capabilities.
